record.original_question: For a one-dimensional real-valued function f of bounded variation, let M be the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. Must the total variation decrease under M, in the sharp form Var(M f) <= Var(f)? If that sharp inequality fails, can Kurka's existing bound with constant 240004 be substantially improved?

evidence.quote: Question 2. Let f : R → R be a function of bounded variation. Do we have Var (M f) ≤ Var (f)? Or at least, can one substantially improve on Kurka’s constant C = 240004?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function of bounded variation, and let
\[
(Mf)(x) \;=\; \sup_{r>0} \frac{1}{2r}\int_{x-r}^{x+r} |f(y)|\,dy
\]
denote the one-dimensional centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator. The total variation of a function $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is
\[
\operatorname{Var}(g) \;=\; \sup\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^{N} |g(x_i)-g(x_{i-1})| : N\in\mathbb{N},\ x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_N\Big\}.
\]
It is known that there exists a finite constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{Var}(Mf)\le C\operatorname{Var}(f)$ for every $f$ of bounded variation, and the smallest constant for which this has been established is $C=240004$.

(a) Does the sharp inequality
\[
\operatorname{Var}(Mf) \;\le\; \operatorname{Var}(f)
\]
hold for every $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ of bounded variation?

(b) If (a) fails, can the constant $C=240004$ be substantially improved; i.e., determine the smallest constant $C$ for which $\operatorname{Var}(Mf)\le C\operatorname{Var}(f)$ holds for all $f$ of bounded variation.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem remains open. Kurka's bound Var(Mf) ≤ 240004 Var(f) (2015) has not been substantially improved for arbitrary BV functions. Bilz and Weigt (arXiv:2107.12404, Journal of Geometric Analysis 2025) proved the sharp inequality Var(Mf) ≤ Var(f) for indicator functions and certain piecewise-constant functions in one dimension, giving partial progress toward the conjectured constant C=1, but the full BV case is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The one-dimensional centred maximal function diminishes the variation of indicator functions
status_evidence.snippet: We prove sharp local and global variation bounds for the centred Hardy–Littlewood maximal functions of indicator functions in one dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp variation bound Var(Mf) ≤ Var(f) is established for indicator functions, providing partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Variation of the centered maximal operator
status_evidence.snippet: Variation of the one-dimensional centered maximal operator on simple functions with gaps between pieces.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress on the sharp constant in the centered BV setting; the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Var(Mf) ≤ 240004 Var(f); whether one can substantially improve Kurka's constant remains a question.
status_evidence.claim: Kurka's constant 240004 is the best known general bound; substantially improving it is open.
